paper.title: Algorithm 425: Generation of Random Correlated Normal Variables
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 15(5), May 1972, pp. 355-357 (the archive header says CACM; the frame lists it under TOMS/CALGO 425.gz, so the venue is recorded as the archive states it). Paper text not checked: it is paywalled.

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 425.gz (scouted 2026-11-27, sha256 000dc68c060cad2f2941ebf85edb2f762f653b5ed6ed7783e39b53109ec9852b). Shell archive unpacks to Fortran/Sp/Drivers/{Makefile,driver.f,res} and Fortran/Sp/Src/src.f. Uses a Lewis-Goodman-Miller style seeded generator (RN in src.f); no external RNG.

claim.location: Shipped reference file Fortran/Sp/Drivers/res (inside 425.gz): the printed output of driver.f subroutine TEST02, which calls RNVR on a 2x2 covariance matrix with off-diagonal 0.3 and the fixed seed iarg=123456789, for 10 samples of dimension 2.
claim.metric: The 20 printed variates of TEST02 (10 samples x 2 components), as printed with format g14.6 in res, read in order (sample, then component).
claim.paper_value: Not located in the paper text (paywalled). The archive's res file is the only value to check.

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The reference prints 6 significant digits (g14.6), so the largest rounding in the printed value is about 5e-6 at magnitude 1. A tolerance of 1e-5 allows one unit in the last printed place, for a single-precision rounding flip, but not a different random sequence or a different covariance transform. Not loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute (30 variates of dimension 2 across 3 tests; the driver runs all 3, TEST02 is the one claimed). Needs a Fortran 77/90 compiler; gfortran is not on this host's PATH, so the rerun must install one.
cost.data_licence: Not stated in the archive; the algorithm is a CACM algorithm published with the ACM, and the rerun should record the licence it finds.

why: The shipped driver's printed output is a seeded run of the algorithm, so the correlated variates depend on the RNVR transform and cannot be read off the code.
